title: Chapter 31
text: ∫ terminology my other favorite cat seemed to be dying and I had him in and out of the vet’s place for x-rays, consultations, injections, operations, “anything at all,” I told the doc, “let’s try to keep him going . . .” one morning I drove over to pick him up and the girl at the counter a vast girl in a wrap-around white nurse’s outfit asked me, “do you want your cat put to sleep?” “what?” I asked. she repeated her statement. “put to sleep?” I asked, “you mean exterminated ?” “well, yes,” she smiled under her tiny eyes, then looking at the card in her hand she said, “oh no, I see it was Mrs. Evans who wanted it done to her cat . . .” “really?” I asked. “I’m sorry,” she said. she walked into the other room with her card and I thought, you’re sorry and I’m sorry, and your sorry fat ass your sorry walk your sorry bed your sorry life and your sorry death and your sorry Mrs. Evans and both of your sorry fat shits. then I walked over, sat down and opened up a cat magazine, then closed it, thinking, it’s just her job; it’s done. she doesn’t kill the cats, she records the messages. when she came out into the office she no longer quite disgusted me and I opened the cat magazine again and turned the pages as if I had forgotten everything, which I hadn’t, exactly.
